purpose: A run of large media-split bands that pile up under the site header as the page scrolls, each a centered claim with an outlined "learn more" button beside its picture, the whole band linking through. An optional large centered section title opens the run. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'media-split-stack', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `band-stack`, `media-split`, `illustration`, `product-widget`, `diagram` and `button`. A band's picture is one of four things: a `ProductWidget` console mock (`widget`), a `Diagram` request-flow figure (`diagram`), a registry `illustration`, or an `image` URL, plain or `imageFramed` on its own plate. `kind` picks the layout only: `media-end` sets every picture at the closing end, `alternating` starts it at the opening end and swaps sides band by band; the bands keep the same shape in both.
useWhen: To list the solution areas or the claims of a page, one large band each, with a link through to its own page.
avoidWhen: For a single claim beside its media → use `media-split` directly.
For small reasons in a grid → use `feature-tiles`.
related: band-stack` — the sticky run the bands pile up in.
media-split` — the band each entry renders through.
bestPractices: Give a band one picture: `widget` (a `ProductWidget` name — the product's console screen), `diagram` (a `Diagram` name — its request flow), `illustration` (a registry name, with `illustrationLabel`) or `image` (a URL, with `imageAlt` when it says something). When several are set the first in that order wins; a band with none renders without its media cell.
Prefer `widget` or `diagram` on a product page: they show the product itself, where an illustration only evokes it. Do not drop to `media-split` and its `media` slot to place one.

Set `imageFramed` for a picture that is an object rather than a scene — a badge, a logo, a screenshot: it sits whole on a rounded, bordered plate inset in the cell. A plain `image` is scaled to fit the cell and never overflows it.
Give every band an `action`; it is both the button and the link the whole band follows.
